given: a SKU's par level is not tracked
when: a warehouse operator opens the detail view for that SKU
then: the par level shows an explicit "not tracked" indication instead of a blank region or a null-related crash
architectural_notes: E2E path over the JSON boundary (R5/NFR-F1-5, NFR-F1-8). Layer split is the load-bearing decision here: the par level is a nullable/optional column (app/models/) read through app/repositories/ -> app/services/; the boundary (app/routes/) returns the record with the par-level field null or omitted and emits NO presentation value. Rendering the explicit "not tracked" indication is owned solely by the React SPA presentation layer (client/) — the boundary must not synthesize a 'not tracked' string. Consequently the R4 branch integration test (NFR-F1-4) for AC3 MUST assert the boundary returns the record with the par-level field absent/null (never that the boundary emits a 'not-tracked indicator'); the explicit indicator and the no-blank/no-crash guarantee are covered by an SPA component test on the untracked path. Pushing the indicator into the boundary would violate the SPA-owns-rendering assignment.

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 cover tracked data present on the record (locations, quantities, tracking code); AC3 covers the untracked optional par-level path, which can be broken (blank region or null crash) while the populated fields still render, and vice versa
